thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: automated page fired for gpu-node-42 (us-west-2a) — reason=kubelet_not_ready, heartbeat_missing=3m, severity=high

pagerduty: PagerDuty: Incident #INC-4892 triggered and sent to on-call. Escalation level 1.

Alex K: acked — taking. I'll grab serial console and check kubelet logs.

Priya S: ack — standing by for impact. Any traffic routed to this node?

Jamal R: seeing a small spike in PodEviction events from the node. Some inference replicas are restarting. Customer-facing inference qps drops ~4% for a short window.

Marcus T: I can run kubectl from jumpbox. Sharing quick checks:
```
kubectl get nodes gpu-node-42 -o wide
kubectl describe node gpu-node-42
journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 80
```

Alex K: attaching serial console now (serial://node-42). Kernel logs show last lines: "kernel: NMI: watchdog: BUG: soft lockup - CPU#3 stuck for 23s" then nothing. Could be kernel hang leading kubelet to stop responding.

sre-runbooks-bot: Runbook suggestion: if node kernel hang + kubelet not ready -> attempt graceful drain if possible, check NVMe SMART, and escalate to DC Ops for physical power reset if serial unresponsive for >5m.

Priya S: customer impact: 3 inference tenants saw elevated 5xxs for ~90s, no broad SLA alert yet. Notifying support to monitor, but looks contained.

DC Ops: received console attach request. Can we try soft-reboot via IPMI first? Confirming serial output is frozen.

DC Ops: on it — initiating IPMI reset in 60s unless you veto. ETA ~2m.

Alex K: hold on with power cycle — let's cordon node and evict eligible pods first to reduce customer impact. If drain stalls due to stuck kubelet, we'll force delete pods and then power-cycle.

Marcus T: running cordon/drain now: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-42 && kubectl drain gpu-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=5m`

incident-bot: drain command started by Marcus T. 12 pods scheduled for eviction. Progress: 4/12 evicted.

pagerduty: Alert: autopager re-fired for gpu-node-42 — ack not processed by incident-bot; action=escalate_to_level2. (This looks like the ack-loop that the system warned about last week.)

Priya S: hmm we're getting duplicate pages despite acks. I suspect pagerduty webhook retries because incident-bot hasn't updated the external status due to network partition to PD.

Marcus T: drain stuck on 8/12 waiting for liveness probes to stop. Some stateful pods refusing eviction. I'll force delete non-critical pods after checking owner refs.

Alex K: go ahead on the non-critical ones. Leave model-serving statefulsets until after power cycle if needed. Keep track of forced-deletes in the incident doc.

Jamal R: marking affected customers: tenant-a (low error budget), tenant-b (dev only). Notifying tenant-a ops: "We are actively mitigating a node outage; brief errors possible."

DC Ops: IPMI reset executed. Node is rebooting. Serial shows POST then watchdog messages cleared.

incident-bot: Node returned to network; kubelet reconnect attempt observed. But kubelet shows: "failed to start: corrupted page allocation" in dmesg. NVMe SMART shows increased reallocated sectors.

Marcus T: kernel errors + NVMe hints of hardware. I'm going to set node to unschedulable and mark for RMA if SMART stays flaky.

Priya S: agree. For immediate customer risk, we need to failover any remaining replicas from that rack. I'll trigger model-routing fallback for tenants with low redundancy.

Alex K: follow-up steps: 1) add node to maintenance (Redwood ticket) 2) RMA with on-prem vendor 3) ensure rollouts for tenants with single-replica pods are expanded 4) create postmortem stub.

sre-runbooks-bot: Template: postmortem checklist created at https://wiki/internal/incidents/INC-4892. Add timeline + root cause hypotheses.

pagerduty: Incident #INC-4892 escalated to Level2 (SRE lead).

Priya S: I pushed a config to routing service to avoid gpu-node-42 for 24h. Rolling fallback complete. Monitoring continues.

Jamal R: Support notified tenant-a with a short blurb. No SLA hit expected but we'll keep watch.

Alex K: quick notes for post-ops: autopager ack-loop caused noise — we should add a debounce on PD webhooks when node enters reboot state to avoid duplicate pages.

Marcus T: saving logs and attaching artifacts to incident ticket. I'll also collect SMART logs and kernel oops for RMA.

DC Ops: requested RMA case opened with vendor; case #RMA-2026-77. ETA on swap unit 48h.

incident-bot: Incident marked mitigated for immediate customer impact. Node will be quarantined pending hardware replacement.

Alex K: handing off to infra oncall (Marcus T) for long-term follow-up and postmortem. If anything changes, re-open. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
